title: Point-in-time recovery on newsroom data tables
description:
Ryan 2026-11-03 approved: turn on DynamoDB point-in-time recovery for the newsroom data tables, in Papyrus, so it ships through each site's normal deploy. About 0.22 GB across 7 sites, about 5 cents a month at $0.20 per GB-month. Reason: a bad write to a corpus record could not be restored exactly on 11-03, and these tables hold votes and curation decisions.

In `amplify/site-backend.ts`, set point-in-time recovery on every Amplify Data table through `backend.data.resources.cfnResources.amplifyDynamoDbTables` (`pointInTimeRecovery`). On by default for every site with no site config; a site can't silently lose it. Check the change doesn't replace any table; enabling PITR is an in-place update, and prove that from a synth. Plugin tables stay as they are unless they hold editorial data; list them and say which you left. A synth test asserts every data table has it. Gherkin scenario. Note in `docs/automated-processes.md` and the relevant infra doc what can and can't be restored: 35 days, restore creates a new table, S3 attachments are not covered. Rollout follows the batch rule: Machines on Machines first in its next bump.
